description: Verify that DUT TCP follows Karn's algorithm — preserve RTO doubling across an ACK that acknowledges a previously retransmitted segment (RFC 1122 §4.2.3.1, RFC 6298 §3 / §5)
approach:
[Objective]
Karn's algorithm: don't reset RTO based on the RTT of an acked retransmit (you can't tell which copy generated the ACK). RFC 6298 §5 keeps the doubled RTO until a non-retransmitted segment is acked.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Handshake → DUT sends data → tester drops it → DUT retransmits with RTO_1 doubled.
2. Phase 1 query: TCP_INFO RTO ≥ doubled baseline.
3. Tester ACKs the retransmit.
4. Phase 2 query: TCP_INFO RTO must remain doubled (Karn's preservation).

[Pass condition]
Phase 2 RTO is still ≥ doubled baseline.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_handshake_did_not_complete
• Fail_phase<n>_query_failed
• Fail_no_phase1_retx
• Fail_initial_rto_not_doubled
• Fail_doubling_not_preserved — Karn's violation

verdicts.Pass: DUT preserved doubled RTO across acked retransmit — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_phase1_retx: No phase 1 retransmit observed in kernel
